jurisdiction.venue: Enforcement Directorate, Mumbai Zonal Office-I (Supreme Court Proceedings)

headline: India’s Enforcement Directorate Attaches ₹556.72 Crore in Real Estate Tied to ₹8,852 Crore Holiday-Club Ponzi Probe
deck: Mumbai anti-money-laundering investigators provisionally attached immovable properties linked to Royal Twinkle Star Club and Citrus Check Inns, alleging promoter Om Prakash Goenka’s 87-entity network paid ₹3,077 crore in agent commissions while circulating investor cash.

live_updates.text: E.D. Mumbai Zonal Office-I provisionally attaches immovable properties valued at approximately ₹556.72 crore under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act.
Investigators trace ₹8,852 crore mobilized between 2008 and 2017 through unregistered holiday-membership schemes across more than 87 group entities.
Attachment executed in furtherance of ongoing Supreme Court of India proceedings aimed at safeguarding investor recoveries; probe continues.

street_crime_compare.exec_summary: India's Enforcement Directorate provisionally attached ₹556.72 crore (~$65.5M) in immovable properties under PMLA in its probe of Royal Twinkle Star Club and Citrus Check Inns, which allegedly raised ₹8,852 crore (~$1.04B) without SEBI registration and routed funds across 87+ entities.
street_crime_compare.street_equivalent: Selling ₹1 lakh vacation vouchers to neighbors without a license, spending a third on sales brokers, and paying old voucher holders with new sign-ups
street_crime_compare.street_sentence: Immediate arrest under economic-offenses statutes and property seizure pending trial

sources.title: ED Mumbai Provisionally Attaches Immovable Properties Worth ₹556.72 Crore in Royal Twinkle Star Club and Citrus Check Inns Investigation

interactive_art_spec.caption: The Supreme Court of India in New Delhi. On Nov. 23, the Enforcement Directorate in Mumbai provisionally attached ₹556.72 crore in immovable properties in furtherance of Supreme Court proceedings over the ₹8,852 crore Royal Twinkle Star Club investigation.
